text:
Alex: Quick experiment idea — workspace rightsizing + swap strategy for multi-model co-residency on 80GB A100s. TL;DR: set dynamic per-model workspace caps based on 95th percentile seq-len, prefer low-memory kernels when free_mem < 6GB, and do aggressive KV prefetch for hot prefixes. Want to validate perf & OOM behavior before canary. Thoughts?

Maya: Sounds promising. Do you have recent profiling to show the hot paths (kernel fallback counts, kv miss rate, swap bandwidth)?

Pranav: Pasting a quick profile from yesterday's cohost run (baseline, 4 models packed):
```
summary:
  p50_token_lat: 42ms
  p95_token_lat: 128ms
  gpu_high_water: 62.1GB
  kernel_fallback_count: 134
  kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.18
  swap_bytes_total: 34GB
  oom_count: 3
```
Notes: most OOMs occurred on long chat sessions (seq > 8k). Kernel fallback spikes when workspace > 48GB fragmented.

Sarah: Main worry is CPU overhead from prefetch + extra bookkeeping; we might shift latency to host CPU and hurt throughput when batching is busy. Also batching heuristics interact with workspace caps — small caps could increase kernel switches.

Alex: Agreed. My idea: right-size workspace cap per model to keep average working set within Nth percentile (N=95) and only allow burst temporary overshoot via a soft-reserve that triggers fast eviction (LRU-K on KV + async write to local nvme swap). Also change kernel fallback order: prefer kernels that trade 5-10% throughput for 30% less memory usage when free mem < threshold.

Maya: Proposed sizing pseudo (very rough):
```
for each model:
  sample seq_lengths over last 24h
  cap = percentile(seq_lengths * per_token_workspace, 95) + safety_margin(10%)
  soft_reserve = min(cap * 1.25, max_soft_limit)
apply caps at runtime via allocator soft quota
```
Will also instrument a metric: workspace_effective_utilization = used_workspace / cap.

Pranav: Also we should adjust KV policy: keep hot prefix entries pinned (LRU with hotness counter), prefetch next-K tokens for active sessions up to soft_reserve. Command to run local bench: `./bench_cohost --models modelA,modelB,modelC --seq-dist heavy-tail --kv-prefetch 64`

infra-bot: Perf test scheduled: perf-runner/job/3129 queued (canary namespace) — expected start in 15m.

Alex: Canary plan: 10% cohost pods on canary zone, run for 2h. Monitor: p50/p95 token latency, kernel_fallback_rate, swap_bandwidth, kv_hit_rate, oom_count, cpu_util. Rollout criteria: p95 <= baseline*1.05 and oom_count == 0 for 2h. Rollback on OOMs > 0 or regression >10%.

Maya: Volunteer to run the data collection + dashboards. I'll add perf panels for: kernel_fallback_rate per-model, workspace_effective_utilization, swap_io_per_min, kv_eviction_rate. Created ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8673

Pranav: Ran a small local run with the sizing + fallback change (toy models, 2h):
```
result snapshot:
  p50_token_lat: 40ms (-4.7%)
  p95_token_lat: 120ms (-6.3%)
  kernel_fallback_count: 48 (-64%)
  swap_bytes_total: 29GB (-14%)
  cpu_user: +12%
  oom_count: 1 (one tail session with seq 12k)
```
Log snippet for OOM: `OOM when allocating workspace 10.8GB for modelB at step 1024`

Alex: That single OOM is expected for the first pass. Two quick ideas: 1) shrink prefetch window for sessions that exhibit super-long tails (>10k) until they are promoted to dedicated slot; 2) on OOM path prioritize evicting soft-reserve KV pages (async) before kernel fallback.

Sarah: We need an explicit rollback alert and runbook edit. I'll add an incident rule: trigger on any OOM_count > 0 in canary namespace and also on kernel_fallback_rate spike > 200/min. Runbook should include `kubectl cordon` + `scale down cohost` + revert allocator flag.

Alex: OK — action items: Maya (dashboards + canary run), Pranav (tune prefetch windows and push bench scripts), Sarah (alert + runbook), I'll open PR for allocator + kernel fallback order.

Maya: On it. I'll post graphs after the perf-run completes.

Pranav: pushing bench artifacts to s3: s3://redwood-perf/cohost/1976543210/ — includes logs + flamegraphs.

Alex: If canary looks clean we'll roll to 50% next week and test burst scenarios. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Sarah: 👍

Alex: Closing this thread — follow-ups in INF-8673 and the PR.
